text:
Anu: Quick one 11 customer demo: stream UI shows garbled mid-response after flaky network, then a second completion arrives.
Rashmi (qa): Repro on iOS WKWebView: open demo, send a long prompt, then quickly background app -> foreground (~500ms). Happens 3/5 runs.
Tom: Which streaming plumbing? EventSource or fetch+ReadableStream?
Anu: fetch + ReadableStream. We chunk by CRLFs and pass lines to JSON.parse. Using TextDecoder streaming mode.
Nate: Two likely failure modes: (1) partial UTF-8 codepoint split across chunks -> JSON.parse blows up; (2) reconnect replay delivers overlapping sequences and UI renders duplicates.
Rashmi (qa): Logs show a comment line right before disconnect: `: resume_id=xyz seq=128`. After reconnect we got `: resume_id=xyz seq=126` then a strand of chunks that included tokens already rendered.
Tom: Ah, server is replaying from an earlier seq, maybe because server thinks client acked only up to 125. Browser client never reported last_seq. Node SDK had an ack handshake, browser didn't.
Anu: Also saw `SyntaxError` in console occasionally from trying to parse an incomplete JSON delta. We try/catch currently but end up duplicating final token when reconnect happens.
Nate: Proposed fixes: (a) make the browser stream parser resilient to split UTF-8 by keeping a tail bytes buffer and using `TextDecoder.decode(bytes, { stream: true })`; (b) parse SSE comment metadata for `resume_id` and `seq` immediately and surface to the app; (c) on reconnect, drop any partial line and reconcile via seq de-dupe before applying to UI.
Tom: Small patch idea: maintain seenSeqs Set for current session (bounded size). On incoming chunk(s) check seq header and ignore seq in seenSeqs. Also emit an event `seq_gap_detected` if new_seq < last_applied_seq.
Rashmi (qa): For QA we can simulate with chrome network throttle + deliberate Hold/Resume via DevTools. I'll script a harness that toggles `navigator.connection` offline for mobile webview-like timing.
Anu: Could we add an opt-in sample app flag `sseStrictSeq=true` so customers can enable strict ordering behavior? Keep default tolerant to avoid breaking demos.
Nate: Yes, feature flag with telemetry. If strict, client will throw on gap and surface a friendly error to app. If tolerant, client will attempt to de-dupe and stitch.
Tom: Tests: unit for TextDecoder tail handling, unit for seq de-dupe, integration test that injects duplicate `[DONE]` tokens and asserts single completion render. Add an e2e that runs on BrowserStack iOS to reproduce WKWebView edge case.
devex-bot: Created RED-1207: "browser-streaming: handle seq/resume + partial utf8 in fetch-stream wrapper" and assigned to @Tom.
ci-bot: CI will run canary build `browser-runtime@v0.21.3-canary.2` to staging at 02:30 UTC.
Tom: I'll open PR with minimal changes: (1) keep byte tail between decode calls; (2) parse `: resume_id` comments into meta; (3) add small in-memory seenSeq window of 512 entries.
Rashmi (qa): Once PR merged, I'll validate with the harness and upload a capture. If it still repros, I'll include raw bytes + decoded text + seq values.
Anu: Thanks team. Low risk change but should stop the duplicate completions and reduce parse errors. :thumbsup:
